# Creator Systems - Purely Personal
# by Daniel Paul · Purely Personal

The operating mechanics behind the biggest one-person content businesses, distilled into
the Purely Personal house method. Five systems. Each one turns "what should I post?"
from a daily crisis into a mechanical step. Use them inside content-strategy Steps 5 and 7,
and hand the outputs to the writing skills in the suite.

---

## SYSTEM 1 - THE TOPIC-BY-FORMAT GRID

The single most valuable move in solo content: stop generating ideas one at a time.
Generate them as a grid.

**Mechanics:**
- Rows = the client's content pillars (from Step 5). Usually 5 or 6.
- Columns = the five angles (System 2 below plus Proof).
- Every cell = one post concept: pillar + angle = a specific post.

6 pillars x 5 angles = 30 post concepts in one sitting. That is 6 to 7 weeks of posting
at the 2026 cadence (System 5), produced mechanically, all on-strategy because every
concept inherits its pillar's positioning and its angle's job.

**The five columns:**
1. Actionable - how to do the thing
2. Analytical - the numbers, the breakdown, the why-it-works
3. Aspirational - the proof it is possible, the lesson from the climb
4. Anthropological - the human why: fears, excuses, lies people tell themselves
5. Proof - the client's own result or client story with numbers

**Worked mini-grid - 3x3 for a leadership coach** (pillars from her intake: she coaches
new managers promoted from within):

| | Actionable | Analytical | Anthropological |
|---|---|---|---|
| **The Promoted Peer Problem** (managing people who were your friends last month) | "The 3-sentence script for your first 1:1 with a former peer. Word for word." | "I tracked 25 internal promotions. 19 lost a friendship in month one. The 6 who didn't all did the same thing first." | "You didn't stop being friends. You started pretending the promotion never happened. That's worse." |
| **Feedback Without Flinching** (new managers who avoid hard conversations) | "How to give critical feedback in under 90 seconds: the 4-line structure I teach every client." | "The average new manager delays a hard conversation 3 weeks. Here's what those 3 weeks cost, in numbers." | "You're not avoiding the conversation to protect them. You're avoiding it to protect how they see you." |
| **The First 90 Days Trap** (proving yourself by doing instead of leading) | "Week one as a manager: the 5 things to stop doing before you start anything new." | "New managers spend 60% of week one on tasks their old role owned. The chart that changed how my clients delegate." | "Nobody promoted you to keep doing your old job better. They promoted you to make it unnecessary." |

Every cell is a publishable post concept with a hook angle built in. That is the standard:
a cell you could hand to linkedin-caption-writer tomorrow.

**The library principle - write from the library, never from the blank page:**
The grid's output is not a to-do list. It is a stocked idea library. Once it exists:
- The client never opens a blank page. They open the library and pick a cell.
- Every published post gets logged: date, pillar, angle, and a 1-10 performance score.
- Winners get republished from a different angle 6 months later (an actionable winner
  returns as its anthropological twin). Losers get one rewrite, then retirement.
- The library compounds. After 90 days the client is choosing from proven material,
  not guessing. This is why prolific creators look effortless: they stopped ideating
  daily years ago.

## SYSTEM 2 - THE FOUR CONTENT ANGLES

Four ways to write about any topic. Each does a different job in the reader's head:

| Angle | Job | Reader's takeaway |
|---|---|---|
| Actionable | Teach the how | "I can use this today" |
| Analytical | Prove the why with numbers | "This person has done the homework" |
| Aspirational | Show it is possible | "If they did it, I can" |
| Anthropological | Name the hidden human reason | "How did they know that's exactly me" |

**Same topic, four headlines** (topic: pricing, for a coach who helps freelancers raise rates):
- Actionable: "How to raise your rates 40% in one email. The exact 4 lines my clients send."
- Analytical: "I reviewed 30 freelance proposals last quarter. Every one that closed above 5k had these 3 things."
- Aspirational: "Two years ago she charged 80 an hour and apologised for it. Last week she closed a 12k package."
- Anthropological: "Freelancers don't undercharge because of the market. They undercharge because of the mirror."

**Angle balance rule:** Most experts default to 80% actionable because teaching feels safe.
But actionable posts get saves, anthropological posts get comments, aspirational posts get
shares, and analytical posts get authority. A week needs the mix, not the default:
- 2 actionable or analytical (the authority spine)
- 1 aspirational or proof (the belief builder)
- 1 anthropological (the comment magnet - it names what the reader privately feels)

Label every topic in the 90-day plan with its angle. An unlabelled topic is an unfinished topic.

## SYSTEM 3 - THE PILLAR-TO-MICRO CASCADE

The biggest solo creators do not write 5 pieces a week. They write ONE deep piece a week
and cut it five ways. Think once, publish many.

**Mechanics:**
1. One substantial piece per week on the week's focus pillar: a newsletter issue or
   long-form post with a framework, a story, and a takeaway. This is the pillar piece.
2. Mine it for micro content. A good pillar piece contains 5 to 7 extractable units:
   - The framework becomes a document carousel
   - The checklist or step list becomes a cheatsheet
   - Each strong standalone point becomes a text post
   - The story becomes an anthropological or aspirational post
   - The best one-liner becomes a short punchy post
3. Micro content points attention back to the deep piece. The deep piece carries the CTA
   and converts (list signup, DM keyword, call booking).

**Why it works:** The micro posts are discovery, the pillar piece is depth, and depth is
what the 2026 algorithm scores as topic authority (System 5). It also means the client's
thinking happens once a week in one sitting instead of five times a week in a panic.

**Inside this suite, the cascade is a skill chain:**

| Cascade step | Skill to run | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Pillar piece | newsletter-writer | The week's deep piece on the focus pillar |
| Framework cut | linkedin-carousel-builder | Document carousel from the pillar piece's framework |
| Checklist cut | linkedin-cheatsheet-builder | Downloadable cheatsheet from the steps or rules |
| Point cuts | linkedin-caption-writer | 2-3 standalone posts, each labelled with its angle |

One brain dump in, a full week of on-pillar content out. This chain is the "weekly
operating rhythm" delivered in the strategy document.

## SYSTEM 4 - THE DEPTH-NICHE TEST

The positioning school that separates creators who convert from creators who entertain:
own a narrow problem completely rather than a wide category thinly. A creator who owns
"Series B financial diligence" gets the call. A creator who covers "startup finance" gets
the follow. Depth beats breadth because buyers search for their exact problem, not a category.

**Run every pillar through four checks:**

1. **The search test.** When the ICP describes this problem in their own words (Step 2,
   Search 2 phrases), is this client the obvious answer? If three other creators would
   come to mind first, the pillar is too wide.
2. **The referral sentence test.** Can a stranger repeat the position in one sentence:
   "She's the one who [specific outcome] for [specific person]." If the sentence needs
   an "and" or a "but also", narrow it.
3. **The say-no test.** Does this pillar visibly exclude some plausible buyers? A pillar
   that excludes nobody attracts nobody. Exclusion is the price of being the obvious choice.
4. **The depth test.** Could the client publish weekly on this pillar for a year without
   repeating themselves? Only pillars anchored in lived experience, a real dataset, or a
   body of client work pass. Opinion-only pillars run dry by week six.

**Scoring:** 4/4 = a power position, keep it. 3/4 = fix the failing check before it ships.
2 or below = it is a category, not a niche. Go one level narrower: add a specific person,
a specific stage, or a specific moment ("pricing" becomes "the first rate rise after
going freelance").

## SYSTEM 5 - CADENCE AND FORMAT MIX, LINKEDIN 2026

What the current data says, and why:

**Cadence: 3-5 posts per week.**
- Moving from 1 post per week to 3+ triggers broader distribution. Past 5, returns diminish
  and quality drops, which now costs more than volume gains, because the algorithm scores
  depth and topic authority over posting streaks.
- One strong post per week beats five forgettable ones. The cascade (System 3) exists so
  the client gets both: one deep think, 4-5 quality outputs.

**Format mix, ranked by current performance:**
- Document carousels: the top format, roughly 1.3-1.4x the reach and engagement of baseline
  posts. Best for frameworks and step lists. Run linkedin-carousel-builder weekly.
- Short vertical video, 30-90 seconds with captions: strong and growing. Long video reach
  has fallen because completion rates are low. Only recommend video if the client will
  actually record it.
- Text-only posts: lowest raw engagement (around 2%) but cheapest to produce and the best
  vehicle for anthropological and story posts, where a document format would kill intimacy.
- External links: cut reach by roughly half or more. Keep links out of the post body.
  Put the link in the first comment or use a DM keyword CTA instead.

**Format rotation:** Posting the same format twice in a row suppresses reach (around 20%).
The weekly rhythm alternates carousel, text, cheatsheet, text by design, so rotation
happens without the client thinking about it.

**Timing:** Tuesday to Thursday, mornings in the audience's timezone, carries the best
averages. But consistency of days beats perfection of hours. Pick 4 fixed days and hold them.

**The 15-minute rule:** Engagement in the 15 minutes after posting (replying to early
comments, commenting on ICP posts) widens initial distribution. Build it into the daily
rhythm as a fixed appointment, not an intention.

---

## HOW THE FIVE SYSTEMS CHAIN TOGETHER

1. Step 5 builds pillars, System 4 sharpens them until each one is a power position.
2. System 1 crosses those pillars with System 2's angles: the grid produces the Month-1
   topic list mechanically, every topic angle-labelled.
3. System 3 turns each week's focus pillar into a full week of output through the suite's
   writing skills.
4. System 5 sets when it ships and in what format.

The client's experience: no blank pages, no "what should I post today", no strategy that
dies in a document. A grid to pick from, a rhythm to run, and skills that do the writing.
